item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 19, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
Ella Langley was the big winner at last night's 60th Annual CMA Awards in Nashville, taking home six awards, including Entertainer of the Year. Taylor Swift returned to the CMA stage after 13 years, while Lainey Wilson and Vince Gill honored Dolly Parton. Brooks & Dunn received the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award. See the complete list of winners and performance highlights at Media Jobs Report dot com.
In audience ratings news,
Eastlan Ratings is expanding into four additional radio markets, including Kansas City, Minneapolis, Nashville and the Lebanon-Hanover-White River Junction region. The company is also moving to continuous audience measurement in Bryan-College Station, Texas. Eastlan President Mike Gould says broadcasters and advertisers deserve a more complete picture of radio listenership.
Turning to television,
NBC is bringing holiday magic to Rockefeller Center on December second. Cynthia Erivo will host and perform during the live Christmas tree lighting special, joined by Kelly Clarkson, Wynonna Judd, Brad Paisley, Alanis Morissette and more. The celebration airs at 8 Eastern on NBC and Peacock.
In radio news,
Audacy's 99.5 The Mountain raised $121,000 during its ninth annual Project Sanctuary Radiothon. Afternoon Host and Brand Manager Dan Hardee led the 12-hour broadcast, sharing stories from veterans and their families. The funds will support therapeutic retreats, counseling and family programs for military and first responder families.
On the education front,
The Broadcasters Foundation of America is expanding its college scholarship program to support more future media professionals. Seven students will receive a combined $25,000 annually, including six new scholarships that no longer require family ties to broadcasting. Applications reopen in spring 2027.
In media technology news,
Amagi is bringing cloud-based live news production to Spectrum News, beginning with Bay News 9 in Tampa and News 13 in Orlando. The technology will eventually support more than 50 feeds across over 35 markets, helping newsrooms get breaking stories on the air faster while streamlining production and master control operations.
Elsewhere in public broadcasting,
WNYC Studios has named veteran science journalist Molly Webster as the new Co-Host of Radiolab, joining Latif Nasser. Webster has spent 14 years with the program and succeeds Lulu Miller, who will focus on the children's podcast Terrestrials. The announcement comes as Radiolab prepares to celebrate its 25th anniversary in 2027.
In music news,
Universal Music Group has named Ignacio Meyer President of Universal Music Latin America and Iberian Peninsula. Meyer joins UMG after more than 15 years at TelevisaUnivision, most recently serving as President of U.S. Networks and Local Media. He will report to newly appointed division CEO Felipe Holguin and focus on artist development, creative strategy and expanding the global reach of Latin music.
And finally,
What makes a great radio personality? It's more than a great voice or playing the right music. It's about building relationships that keep listeners coming back. In a new blog, Brian Wright of Wright Media Group shares 14 ways radio personalities can build trust, connect with their audience, and turn casual listeners into loyal fans. Discover why lasting relationships are the key to success in radio. Read Brian's full blog now at Media Jobs Report dot com.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
